html:
A Chinese writer, born Zhou Shuren, who is seen as the founder of modern Chinese literature. His stories and essays, in plain spoken Chinese, attacked the cruelty and blindness of the old society.

He grew up in Shaoxing in a declining scholar family. He went to Japan to study medicine. He later wrote that a lantern slide shown in class, of Chinese bystanders calmly watching a Chinese man about to be executed by Japanese soldiers, made him decide that China's spirit needed healing more than its bodies, and he turned to writing.

In 1918 he published "A Madman's Diary", one of the first major stories in vernacular Chinese, in the magazine that led the New Culture Movement. It and "The True Story of Ah Q" became classics of the May Fourth era. He later wrote mainly biting essays and led left-wing writers in Shanghai, though he never joined the Communist Party.

After his death in 1936, Mao Zedong hailed him as a hero of the revolution, and his works were taught to every Chinese schoolchild.
